builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Training Small Language Models for Transferable Tool Selection
summary: The method replaces reliance on proprietary commercial LLMs (Claude/ChatGPT) to decompose instructions and drive retrieval-based tool selection with a small open model post-trained via reinforcement learning. The cost is an RL post-training pipeline with its reward design and training data for an 8B model, plus ongoing maintenance as the tool corpus evolves. It can fail if the reward signal does not capture which tools are actually needed for multi-step instructions, if the claimed transfer to new retrievers and domains does not hold for the reader's specific tool corpus, or if RL training instability makes the recipe hard to reproduce.
rationale: A small open model replacing paid frontier-model calls for tool routing fits the constrained budget, but the RL training recipe and its transfer claims require validation on the reader's own tool corpus before production adoption.
technique: RL-trained small model for tool selection

claims.statement: The method replaces reliance on proprietary commercial LLMs (Claude/ChatGPT) to decompose instructions and drive retrieval-based tool selection with a small open model post-trained via reinforcement learning. The cost is an RL post-training pipeline with its reward design and training data for an 8B model, plus ongoing maintenance as the tool corpus evolves. It can fail if the reward signal does not capture which tools are actually needed for multi-step instructions, if the claimed transfer to new retrievers and domains does not hold for the reader's specific tool corpus, or if RL training instability makes the recipe hard to reproduce.
A Qwen3-8B model post-trained with the paper's RL recipe outperforms Llama-4-Maverick (402B) on ToolBench tool selection, and transfers to different retrievers and new tool corpora.
